title: Image-adoration is called ‘honorary’—outward honor-signs; refuse them and you are a hypocrite even if you claim to ‘venerate’
source_text: X. Istam autem adorationem quam imaginibus deberi existimant, & a cultu latriae distinguunt, honorariam vocant, & docent esse honoris emphasim, seu demonstrationem, prout habetur in verbis Anastasii Episcopi Theopoleos, jam supra memoratis, Quid enim aliud est, inquit, quam honoris alicui exhibiti, veluti emphasis adoratio? Istam autem honorationis emphasim constituunt in externis quibusdam honoris signis atque testimoniis, quae si quis imaginibus Christi & sanctorum deferre recuset, illum habent pro hypocrita, etiamsi alioqui eas se venerari, id est, reverenter habere profiteatur. Ut videre est in Tharasii verbis, quae subjuncta sunt verbis Anastasii, & supra fuerunt a nobis relata.
pass_a_gloss: But that adoration which they think is owed to images, and which they distinguish from the cult of latria, they call honorary, and they teach that it is an emphasis or demonstration of honor, as is had in the words of Anastasius Bishop of Theopolis already recalled above: For what else is adoration, he says, than as it were an emphasis of honor exhibited to someone? But that emphasis of honoring they constitute in certain outward signs and testimonies of honor, which if anyone refuses to pay to the images of Christ and of the saints, they hold him for a hypocrite, even if otherwise he professes that he venerates them, that is, holds them reverently. As may be seen in Tarasius’s words, which were subjoined to Anastasius’s words and were related by us above.
pass_b_english: They brand image-adoration ‘honorary’—an outward emphasis of honor, not latria.
Kiss, bow, and the other signs are required; refuse them while claiming ‘veneration’ and you are still a hypocrite.

choices.why: Defines the required external acts of image-honor.
